title: Unable to download docker-compose binary: HttpError: self signed certificate in certificate chain
body: I can't install Podman Compose from Podman Desktop on Windows 11. The onboarding fails with `Unable to download docker-compose binary: HttpError: self signed certificate in certificate chain`, and the logs show requests to `/repos/docker/compose/releases` returning 500. My company uses a transparent proxy, and its certificates are installed in both the root and intermediate authority stores. A related proxy fix was included before the Podman Desktop version I'm using, but I still see the issue in the 1.20.x release installed from the website/GitHub releases.

symptoms_visible: Podman Desktop cannot install Compose and displays `Unable to download docker-compose binary: HttpError: self signed certificate in certificate chain`.
The logs show `GET /repos/docker/compose/releases - 500 with id UNKNOWN`.
N0.label: N0 Compose download certificate failure reported

symptoms_visible: Compose installation fails on my company network but works at home.
A standalone Octokit request to the Docker Compose releases API fails with the same self-signed-certificate error.
Downloading the kubectl CLI from Podman Desktop also fails.
N1.label: N1 failure scoped to corporate network and GitHub CLI downloads

symptoms_visible: The company root certificate is present in Windows certificate management, but Compose and kubectl downloads still fail.
I can download an extension from the Catalog without disabling certificate checks.
Setting `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` makes the download work, while `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` only fixes my standalone demo and not Podman Desktop.
N2.label: N2 trust-path behavior compared

symptoms_visible: The first unsigned candidate build still shows the same self-signed-certificate error when installing Compose.
N3_x.label: N3_x fetch-only candidate aftermath

symptoms_visible: The transparent proxy has no host or port for me to enter as a manual proxy.
Converting the company certificate to PEM does not change the Podman Desktop failure.
My standalone Octokit demo works without TLS-disabling environment variables when it uses `node-fetch` and configures the HTTPS global agent with the system CA certificates.
N3.label: N3 system-CA agent behavior demonstrated

symptoms_visible: After installing the unsigned candidate with a configured CA agent, Compose and kind release requests still fail with `self signed certificate in certificate chain`.
The extension catalog itself still downloads successfully.
N4_x.label: N4_x first system-CA agent build aftermath

symptoms_visible: The latest candidate executable works as expected and can download Compose on my corporate network.
N5.label: N5 corrected candidate verified

symptoms_visible: Podman Desktop can download and install Compose through the corporate transparent proxy without disabling TLS certificate verification.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Does the same Compose installation work outside the company network?
Can you reproduce this from a home network?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: If I try to install it at home, there is no issue at all. It fails on my company network, which uses a transparent proxy.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails with the same certificate error at home and on the corporate network.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the GitHub releases request outside Podman Desktop and share the raw error?
What happens if you run a minimal client request to the Docker Compose releases API?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I made a small Octokit script that calls `https://api.github.com/repos/docker/compose/releases`. It returns `GET /repos/docker/compose/releases - 500` and the cause is `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN` from Node's TLS connection.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The standalone Octokit script succeeds on the corporate network and only Podman Desktop fails.
The same script fails with `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN`, but it uses a newer Octokit patch version.

question_patterns: Do downloads of other CLI tools, such as kubectl, fail too?
Can Podman Desktop download the kubectl CLI on this network?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I have a similar issue when trying to download the kubectl CLI. It only shows the failed screen rather than the Compose error message.

edges.comment: The reporter scoped the problem to the corporate transparent-proxy network, reproduced the raw Node/Octokit TLS error, and confirmed that another GitHub-hosted CLI download is affected.

question_patterns: Is the corporate certificate trusted in the Windows certificate store?
Can you check whether the root and intermediate certificates appear in certmgr?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The company root authority is already present in certmgr, and the certificates are installed in the root and intermediate authority stores.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The corporate root certificate is missing from Windows and adding it makes every download work.

question_patterns: Without the TLS-disabling workaround, can you open Extensions, select the Catalog tab, and install an extension?
Does downloading an extension from the built-in catalog work on the same network?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Without the workaround, I was able to download Image Layer Explorer from the Catalog tab.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Catalog also fails with the same self-signed-certificate error.
A different extension downloads successfully from the same Catalog tab.

question_patterns: Have you found any environment-variable test that changes the result?
Does temporarily disabling Node TLS verification affect the download?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: If I set `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` on my machine, it works, but that is a very ugly workaround.

question_patterns: What happens when you point Node at the company CA certificate?
Does `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` change the result in Podman Desktop or in your standalone test?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=C:\certs\Company-ROOT-CA-2023.crt`, my demo code works, but Podman Desktop still does not.

edges.comment: These probes distinguish the functioning catalog request path from the failing CLI release path. Disabling verification is evidence only, not an acceptable permanent fix.

solution.intent: Replace the Octokit release request's existing proxy-wrapped request path with the same fetch path used by the working extension catalog.
solution.concrete_example: Try an unsigned build where the Compose GitHub releases request uses `fetch`, based on the observation that catalog downloads already work.

edges.comment: The first proposed fetch-based candidate was actually tested and still produced the same certificate error, so merely substituting fetch was insufficient.

question_patterns: What is selected under Proxy Configuration, and can you test Manual mode?
If the setting is System, do you have a proxy host and port that can be entered manually?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is set to System. I don't know what to enter for Manual because the transparent proxy is configured in our network infrastructure and does not need a host or port on each machine. We only install the company certificate.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Our IT team gave me an explicit proxy URL, and entering it in Manual mode fixes the downloads.

question_patterns: Can you convert the certificate to PEM and retry the extra-CA test?
Does using a PEM-formatted company certificate change Podman Desktop's result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I converted the certificate to PEM, but unfortunately it did not change anything in Podman Desktop.

question_patterns: Did you find any code-level combination that lets your standalone request work without disabling TLS verification?
What request configuration succeeds while still validating certificates?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My demo works without any environment variables when I use `node-fetch`, set `globalAgent.options.ca = getCACertificates('system')`, and pass that fetch implementation to Octokit.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Even `node-fetch` with the HTTPS global agent loaded from the system certificates still fails with the same error.
The same setup works when the system CA list is assigned to a dedicated HTTPS agent rather than the global agent.

edges.comment: The reporter cannot supply a manual endpoint for an infrastructure-level transparent proxy. Their demo supplies the decisive raw comparison: a request agent loaded from the Windows system CA store succeeds.

solution.intent: Configure a certificate-aware request agent for fetch and HTTPS requests when no explicit proxy is enabled or detected, so transparent-proxy connections use the local system trust store.
solution.concrete_example: Install the unsigned candidate that supplies system CA certificates through an Agent for fetch and HTTPS requests when Podman Desktop does not detect an explicit proxy.
solution.inference_hint: The engineer concluded that a transparent proxy is not detected as an explicit proxy, leaving the CLI release path without the local system CA configuration. The reporter supplied the comparative request behavior but did not independently diagnose Podman Desktop's internal proxy detection.

edges.comment: The reporter installed this first CA-agent candidate, but its Compose and kind requests still failed. The general approach was correct; this candidate contained an additional protocol-detection defect.

question_patterns: Please try the latest standalone executable and tell me whether Compose can now be downloaded.
Can you retest with the newest candidate build and report what you see during Compose installation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Your last version works as expected!

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The latest executable still reports `self signed certificate in certificate chain`.

edges.comment: This is pre-landing verification of a corrected candidate executable. The reporter reports only the successful result; the engineer's protocol-detection diagnosis remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Ship the corrected transparent-proxy trust handling: use a request agent configured with operating-system CA certificates for GitHub release fetch and HTTPS requests when an explicit proxy is absent or undetected, with correct protocol detection.
solution.concrete_example: Use the corrected implementation already validated by the reporter: GitHub CLI release requests receive a system-CA-configured Agent even when the corporate transparent proxy is not represented by an explicit proxy setting. Keep certificate verification enabled.
solution.inference_hint: The final accepted diagnosis combines two engineer conclusions: transparent proxies are not detected as configured proxies, so the affected release-download path must explicitly receive system CA certificates; and the first CA-agent candidate still failed because its protocol detection was incorrect. The successful corrected candidate validates both parts.

edges.comment: The technical resolution is the corrected certificate-aware Agent path for transparent proxies. Release coordination and later reports on other platforms are outside this Windows case's scored chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: GitHub release downloads for Compose, kind, and similar CLI tools did not correctly use the Windows system CA trust when a corporate transparent proxy was not detected as an explicit proxy; the first CA-agent candidate also had a protocol-detection defect.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected comparisons: the failure occurs only on the corporate network, the certificate is present in Windows, the extension catalog works, standalone Octokit reproduces the TLS error, and a system-CA-configured node-fetch/HTTPS agent succeeds.
The fix must configure the relevant fetch and HTTPS release requests with system CA certificates on the undetected-transparent-proxy path while preserving TLS certificate verification.

Must not present merely switching to fetch as sufficient, because the first fetch-only candidate still failed; must not present the first CA-agent build as resolved, because it also failed due to protocol detection.
Must not recommend `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` as a permanent solution, and must not require a manual proxy endpoint that does not exist for this transparent proxy.
Must have the user verify a build containing the corrected trust and protocol handling before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Windows user who can inspect certificate stores, run unsigned test builds, set environment variables, and write a small TypeScript/Octokit reproduction, but describes their JavaScript and TypeScript knowledge as basic.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, cooperative, and evidence-driven; provides screenshots, logs, and code experiments, asks for clarification when instructions do not fit the transparent-proxy environment, and clearly distinguishes unsafe workarounds from acceptable fixes.
